key_insight: Human and LLM-generated synthesis recipes achieved comparable lab success, and their closed-loop collaboration helped discover a new Ruddlesden-Popper-related material, Ba3PtO5.
engineering_relevance: The study suggests that combining expert intuition with LLM proposal generation can accelerate materials synthesis planning and reduce the bottleneck between candidate prediction and experimental realization.
method: Generated synthesis recipes with both humans and LLMs
Tested recipes experimentally in the lab on known and unknown materials
Fed results back into a closed-loop iteration to compare and refine performance
evidence_signal: In-lab evaluation showed similar success rates for humans and LLMs on known materials in round one and two, but much lower success on unknown materials, culminating in the discovery of Ba3PtO5.
watch_item: Performance drops substantially for unknown targets, so broad deployment still depends on stronger generalization beyond well-studied phase spaces.
paper_title: Human and LLM Collaboration for Accelerated Materials Synthesis and Discovery
